the two recombinant domains of CD55 crystallized in a monoclinic crystal form and a native data-set has been collected to 1.6 A resolution.
we have crystallized two of the four short consensus repeat domains of CD55 and collected a data set to 165 A resolution.
we have crystallized two domains of CD55 and have obtained a native data set at a synchrotron facility.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structure and function of a protein that is involved in complement regulation and in viral and bacterial pathogenesis.
the structure and function of the short consensus repeat (SRC) domains of the complement regulatory proteins CD55 (decay accelerating factor) and CD46 (membrane cofactor protein).
the structural biology of a key regulator of the complement cascade.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the crystal structure of the CD55 SCR domain has been determined to 1.6 A resolution.
the two SCR domains of CD 55, expressed in yeast, have been successfully crystallized.
the crystallization of CD55 is a significant achievement.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
this is the first report for the crystallization of a SCR containing protein.
we have crystallized the first SCR domain containing protein, which is biologically active and has a well ordered structure.

we have successfully expressed and purified a fragment of CD55, which is a biologically active receptor of the virus echovirus 11, in a recombinant expression system and have crystallized the fragment.

a short consensus repeat domain can be crystallized as a monomer.
it has been possible to crystallize a fragment of CD55, which retains the biological function of binding to a virus, and that this has been possible using a simple and rapid protocol.
